messages:
sahil: noticing a sudden spike in inference QPS from prod-us-east-1 at 12:52 UTC, p95 latency climbed from 180ms -> 900ms. Autoscaler didn't add GPU nodes. logs show quota errors and provisioning retries.

maria: saw it too, forwarded Cloud provider alert: "QuotaExceeded: requested GPUs > quota for region us-east-1". link: https://console.example.cloud/alerts/INC-8132 :warning:

jen: ops-bot shows nodepool gpu-pool-us-east stuck in PROVISIONING -> FAILED -> RETRY loop. Autoscaler reported "scale request accepted" but no new nodes registered.

ops-bot: [autoscaler] scale_request: {pool: gpu-pool-us-east, want: +8} -> submit_provision -> provider_error: QuotaExceeded -> backoff 30s -> retry_count=6

liam: digging into autoscaler metrics: scale-up requests are being suppressed by cooldown and perceived thrash. We got multiple transient traffic spikes (spike bursts) so cooldown logic thinks we are in a flapping state.

sahil: example logs from the controller: ```
2026-05-14T12:52:03Z INFO scaleQueue.add requestId=abc123 want=8
2026-05-14T12:52:05Z ERROR provider.Provision failed region=us-east-1 reason=QuotaExceeded
2026-05-14T12:52:35Z INFO scaleQueue.backoff duration=30s retry=1
2026-05-14T12:53:10Z INFO cooldown: suppressing further requests for pool=gpu-pool-us-east ttl=300s
```

maria: can we failover traffic to eu-west-1 or to Dedicated capacity? We have spare dedicated in eu-west with headroom. Might add cross-region latency but keeps SLO.

jen: propose immediate mitigation: 1) Flip routing flag to route new sessions from prod-us-east-1 -> eu-west-1 dedicated pool (feature-flag: ff.route.east.to.eu) 2) Manually increase reserved capacity in eu-west dedicated by +50 GPUs 3) Pause autoscaler's cooldown suppression for 10m for this incident.

liam: I'm worried about cost on dedicated bump. How long we expect spillover? If spike is ~15m we can tolerate cost. If longer, we should create a cheaper fallback (smaller quantized model) as auto-fallback.

oncall: I patched the routing flag and opened a manual capacity increase request to cloud console (request id: req-9921). Traffic shift is live — watching telemetry. :eyes:

deploy-bot: traffic switch: route-rule ff.route.east.to.eu = true -> applied.

maria: after shift p95 dropped from 900ms -> 220ms for routed sessions. There are still some queued requests hitting the original pool while retries in flight.

jen: manual cloud response: provider accepted capacity increase in eu-west, new nodes starting, ETA ~7m. Provider note: us-east quota is at limit due to recent experiments; we need formal quota request to raise permanently.

liam: action items: - open quota increase ticket for us-east (maria) - add metric to detect 'quota_exceeded' provider errors and mark pool as "provider-blocked" to trigger immediate cross-region failover (jen) - add synthetic spike tests to simulate bursty traffic and verify cooldown logic (sahil) - cleanup: document cost threshold for dedicated bump (finance sync)

maria: filed provider ticket INC-8420 for quota bump and attached experiment inventory. ETA from provider: 48-72h.

sahil: follow-up: we'll shorten cooldown floor from 300s -> 90s for bursty pools as a temporary config and add a guard that allows one emergency manual override to bypass cooldown. jen can you own the config change?

jen: will make the cooldown PR and put it behind a feature flag. target deploy in next 2 hours after smoke tests.

liam: note for postmortem: autoscaler should differentiate provider errors vs real provision lag. Quota errors must be treated as permanent until operator clears them, not as transient thrash.

oncall: monitoring update: added dashboard tile for provider_error_rate and routing-failover_count. Saved runbook steps in https://playbook.internal/redwood/infra/failover-gpu.

sahil: thanks team. current state: traffic routed to eu-west dedicated, nodes launching, p95 stabilizing. We'll keep this thread updated until quota uplift completed and us-east healed. :thumbsup:
